APPRAISAL COMMENTARY

40 Hood Avenue, Earlwood is a three-bedroom, one-bathroom house with parking for four cars on a 430 sqm block. This commentary sets out the comparable sales and market data behind the estimated value of $2,343,000, so you can assess the asking price with confidence.

The closest match is 8 Eulabah Avenue, a three-bedroom, one-bathroom, four-car home on 404 sqm, which sold for $1,960,000 in February 2025, the lowest result. 8B Nelson Road, with the same layout on 1112 sqm, sold for $1,980,000, but that was in June 2021. More recent sales sit higher: 26 William Street, a two-bathroom home on 708 sqm, sold for $2,210,000 in June 2026, while 5A Dellwood Avenue, on 720 sqm, sold for $2,800,000 and 157 Riverview Road, on 600 sqm, sold for $2,765,000, both in March 2026. The evidence ranges from $1,960,000 to $2,800,000, and the estimate sits above the closest match.

Earlwood's market has cooled. The suburb median is $2,080,000, prices are down 17% over the year and 3.5% in the past month, and homes sell in a median of 27 days. The auction clearance rate is 58.6%, vacancy is 1.11% and rental yield is 2.7%.

For a buyer, the estimate is driven by larger-block sales. With prices falling, there is a good case to offer closer to the 8 Eulabah Avenue result.

AFFORDABILITY ASSESSMENT

Based on a gross annual income of $90,096, a partner income of $90,410 and an available deposit of $197,219, your estimated borrowing capacity is $911,169, with a maximum loan amount of $713,950. This capacity combines your deposit with the maximum loan and assumes repayments of 30% of your income. On these figures, the estimated value of $2,343,000 is far beyond your borrowing capacity. A house in Earlwood is not achievable on your current finances. Apartments in Earlwood or houses in more affordable suburbs would better match your budget, and a lender can help you plan.

20 Blue Gum Street, Nambucca Heads is a three-bedroom, one-bathroom house with a single car space on a 753 sqm block. This commentary reviews the sales evidence and market conditions behind the estimated value of $734,600, to help you decide whether the price is right.

The closest in land size is 8 Glen Sheather Drive, on 712 sqm, which sold for $770,000 in June 2026. 22 Centenary Parade, on 660 sqm, sold for $625,000 in March 2026, the lowest result, and 105 Seaview Street, on 573 sqm, sold for $703,000 in February 2026. 3 Ibis Court, on 488 sqm, sold for $650,000 in November 2025. The highest is 2A Lackey Street, a two-car home on 582 sqm, which sold for $925,000 in April 2026. The evidence ranges from $625,000 to $925,000, and the estimate sits just below the closest match.

Nambucca Heads is a steady coastal market. The suburb median is $765,000, with 9% annual growth and no change in the past month. Homes take a median of 55 days to sell, vacancy is 2.09%, rental yield is 4.52%, and the 0% clearance rate shows sales are negotiated privately.

For a buyer, $734,600 is a fair benchmark. Longer selling times mean you can take your time and negotiate.

AFFORDABILITY ASSESSMENT

Based on a gross annual income of $135,737, a partner income of $50,397 and an available deposit of $71,181, your estimated borrowing capacity is $807,391, with a maximum loan amount of $736,210. This capacity combines your deposit with the maximum loan and assumes repayments of 30% of your income. On these figures, the estimated value of $734,600 sits within your borrowing capacity. You should be able to purchase this property, though it would use most of what you can borrow. With a modest deposit, budget for stamp duty and possibly lenders mortgage insurance, and confirm the figures with your lender before you make an offer.

The evidence spans $740,000 to $1,100,000, and the estimate sits just above the main cluster of sales.

Raymond Terrace is a strong market. The suburb median is $740,000, with 24% annual growth and 2.5% growth in the past month. Homes sell in a median of just 20 days, vacancy is 1.07%, rental yield is 4.43%, and the 0% clearance rate shows sales are negotiated privately.

For the vendor, a price guide around $868,800 is supported. Quick selling times and strong growth point to good demand, and the July result at 3 Bellevue Street shows what the top of the market can reach.

The suburb median is $2,130,000, and homes are selling in a median of 15 days, with an auction clearance rate of 61.2% and vacancy of just 0.72%. The recorded annual growth of 231% is unusually high and should be read with caution, as monthly growth was 0%.

For an investor, the evidence supports a purchase price close to $2,047,000, though the property's value case rests on capital growth rather than rental income.

At a purchase price of $2,047,000 with a $300,447 deposit and a 6.39% interest rate, the estimated weekly rent of $1,563 delivers a gross rental yield of 3.97% and a net yield of 3.29%. After financing costs, the property is projected to run a monthly shortfall of $6,056, giving a cash-on-cash return of -24.19%. The rent covers only part of the holding costs, so this is a growth-focused investment that needs strong cash reserves. Low vacancy of 0.72% supports reliable tenancy, but the return depends on Penshurst's prices continuing to rise.
